sort.ask: How should the Effect-schema Cmd helper handle schemas whose two sides differ? The downstream trial shows a transformation on `input` never runs (so the acceptance fixture for it can't be observed). It also shows a transforming `ok` schema gets `malformed_result` every time. Should the helper refuse such schemas, or type handlers by the encoded side? And should the helper also cover agent tools in ./agent?
options: Refuse schemas whose two sides differ: use Schema.Codec<T, NoInfer<T>> so they fail to compile (Schema.toType is the way through), drop the input-transformation fixture case, and use the same helper for agent tools
Accept transforming schemas and type the handler by the ok schema's encoded side, so the decode runs at settle; change the input fixture to show the transformation is not applied
Ship the helper for Cmd.define only, exactly as the trial did, and move agent tools and the transformation question to a separate issue
sort.why: This is a new ask from a host of the library, with no duplicate in the backlog. The downstream trial found that one acceptance criterion can't be met and that schemas whose two sides differ break handlers. Choosing between refusing those schemas and retyping handlers changes the public API and the acceptance criteria, so an owner should decide before a builder starts.

sort.ask: Should tea own a typed-port program model (in/out/request ports, payload fit, route graph, defineProgram) that Tuval now builds on its own? If so, where does 'program' end and 'desk' begin, which entry holds it, and what happens to today's definePort? This is weighed against the rulings in #325/#316, #312/#556, ADR 0020 and ADR 0022.
options: Keep the current line: tea exposes primitives only (definePort, fromPort, run/spawn/tell). Tuval keeps its program model, and tea at most documents a how-to recipe.

Move only the port layer into a new Effect-only entry: typed in/out/request port declarations with schemas, the payload-fit check and the queues. The route graph, the registry and defineProgram stay in Tuval.
Move the whole program model, including the route graph and defineProgram, into tea. This reverses or revises the no-registry and no-battery rulings and renames or replaces today's definePort.
sort.why: This is the first time a host has asked tea to own a typed in/out port program model, so a no doesn't fit, but the ticket itself says the request pulls against earlier owner rulings (#325, #312/#556, ADR 0020, ADR 0022). An owner has to set the direction before anything is built. #636's spike is related but asks a narrower question, so this is not a duplicate.

sort.ask: Should tea own a program idea (typed in/out/request ports, payload fit, route graph, defineProgram) so Tuval can become a GUI shell? If it should, where does program end and desk begin, and what happens to today's definePort, given the earlier rulings that tea has no registry or supervisor (#312/#556), does no DI (ADR 0020) and has no battery layer (ADR 0022)?
options: Keep the program model in Tuval. tea only fills gaps in the primitives it already has (Cmd.define as the out/ask port with a runtime input check, a schema for Msgs that arrive from outside, spawn/tell) and the host composes them, as #325 ruled.

Move only the port layer into tea: typed in/out ports over Standard Schema, the payload-fit check and an Elm-style Program unit. Retire or rename definePort. The route graph and registry stay in the host.
Move the full program model into tea (in a new entry or under ./effect), route-graph compile and registry included, and record a new ADR that reverses #312/#556 and ADR 0020 where they conflict.

This is a real bug in shipped code. parseAnswers returns a value typed as having every criteria key in probabilities, but it never checks the keys, so a partial or mis-keyed answer still parses as ok. The fix is clear (a key-totality check against question.criteria plus tests) and it covers a case the jev door work in plan #215 missed.

This is a real bug in shipped code. parseAnswers lets a choice answer whose probabilities keys don't match the criteria pass, even though its type claims every key is there. The fix is clear: a new JevErr variant plus tests, and the comment adds a compile-time check on JEV_ERR_TAGS. #216 and epic #214 are closed, so this is new follow-up work. #215 is a grilling session, not a build plan.

sort.ask: Should tea ship a Cmd-from-Effect-Schema helper in ./effect? If so, what should it do with schemas whose decoded and encoded types differ (transformations, brands)? That choice also decides whether the fixture case with a transforming input schema is dropped, since tea never runs a Cmd's input schema.
options: Ship the helper and refuse transforming or branded schemas at the type level (Schema.Codec<T, NoInfer<T>>, as tea-fabrika does). Drop the input-transformation fixture case and point users to Schema.toType.
Ship the helper and type handlers by the schema's input (encoded) side, so a transforming ok schema works. Keep a transformation fixture for ok only.
Don't add the helper to tea. Document the wrapper pattern in the Effect how-to and leave the helper to hosts.
